answer.summary: Raskin found the hero’s journey too theoretical to guide a pitch, and people tended to glaze over when he used it. Instead, he focused on the structure of one strategic story: show the shift to a new world or “game” and make the person hearing the pitch the main character who can win in it.

sections.heading: What he learned was a mistake
sections.content: Using the hero’s journey as a pitch framework didn’t tell Raskin concretely what to do. He found it too theoretical, and said people seemed to glaze over when he used it, so he stopped talking about it in his work.

sections.heading: What he focused on instead
sections.content: Rather than teaching storytelling as a general skill or centering a hero who has a problem and gets saved, Raskin focused on the structure of one story. It spells out a shift in the world—from an old game to a new one—and turns the person hearing the pitch into the main character: they need to change and can come along to win in the new world. He described this as defining a movement, rather than simply saying, “I’m going to solve your problem.”

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately says the hero’s journey felt too theoretical to guide what to do in a pitch and that people seemed to glaze over. It also explains that Raskin focused instead on the structure of one story, making the person hearing the pitch its main character. These points are supported by the cited context.
